title: JDesk Predictive Install — Native Registry Schema
author: MEARVK LLC
description: Registry file maintained by predictive-install.sh. Tracks all installed natives with version, SHA-256, installer ID, install date, and install count. Used for pre-install check-ahead, delete verification, and reinstall decisions.

1_essential.philosophy: Always installed first. Small footprint, always used. The system cannot function as a desktop without these.

2_productive.philosophy: High utility, moderate size. These are what users sit down to work with every day.

3_connected.philosophy: Internet/network-facing applications. Needed for web work and research.

4_extended.philosophy: Large footprint, optional functionality. Installed only if space permits. High value for specific workflows but not daily necessities.

scoring.utility_range: 1-10 (how useful is this app when you need it)
scoring.probable_use_range: 1-10 (how often will a typical user need it)
scoring.ordering: Within each tier, highest score installs first (best value per MB)

space_behavior.graceful_stop: If space runs out mid-tier, stop and report what was installed vs skipped
space_behavior.never_fills_disk: Always leaves at least 200 MB headroom

registry_fields.name: Human-readable application name
registry_fields.version: Detected version string from --version or equivalent
registry_fields.sha256: SHA-256 of the installed binary (or symlink target)
registry_fields.binary: Path to the installed binary or symlink
registry_fields.installer_id: Identity of the installer tech who ran the install
registry_fields.install_count: Number of times this native has been installed (tracks reinstalls)

check_ahead.description: Before installing any native, the system checks the existing binary
checks: Does the binary exist at the target path?
Is it a symlink? If so, is the target valid?
What is the current SHA-256? Does it match the registry?
Has the binary been modified since install (SHA mismatch)?

decisions.sha_mismatch: Warn (binary was modified outside our control)

steps: 1. Verify the ID exists in our registry
2. Check if the binary is a symlink (safe to remove) or an actual file
3. Only remove within /opt/jdesk/apps/ — refuse to touch system paths
delete_protocol.safety: Will not rm -rf outside /opt/jdesk/apps/. System packages (apt) are only unlinked, not purged.
